heroHeadline: Piracy Crisis Day 30/29/23: Egypt Formally Demands Somalia Help Release MT Eureka Crew — Adan Yabal Day 36 Under Al-Shabaab; ICG Warns of 'Electoral Showdown' as Opposition Countdown Reaches Day 10
heroSubtitle: On May 25, 2026, Somalia's three-vessel piracy crisis entered Day 30/29/23 with all 44 hostages (Honour 25, 17 crew; Sward, 15 crew; MT Eureka, 12 crew) still captive and no ransom or rescue. Egypt formally called on the Federal Government of Somalia to secure MT Eureka's 12 crew members — a new state-to-state escalation. Honour 25 crew conditions remain critical: one daily rice serving, no clean water, medicine exhausted; $3M Pakistan-directed demand and $10M MT Eureka demand unmet. EU NAVFOR Atalanta and CTF-151 counter-piracy assets remain diverted to the Persian Gulf and Red Sea by the Iran War; FDD (May 14) confirmed Iran-backed Houthis provide weapons and GPS to Somali pirates. Al-Shabaab held Adan Yabal in Hiiraan Region for Day 36 — the longest uncontested insurgent occupation of a Hiiraan town since the 2022 SNA/Macawisley offensive — with no counter-offensive despite President Mohamud's April 19 emergency order. ICG released Briefing B208 'Electoral Showdown in Somalia' warning the political deadlock risks another cycle of turmoil; ISS Africa (May 20) flagged 'another election deadline lapsed' as Somalia's political paralysis directly enables Al-Shabaab's territorial consolidation. Puntland hosted a US diplomatic delegation May 20; opposition countdown reaches Day 10. UN News: Somalia faces 'real risk of famine' with 6.5M food-insecure; WFP July 2026 shutdown warning active. AFRICOM strike count: 63+ (last confirmed May 7).
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, OCHA, UNSOM, WFP, FEWS NET, AFRICOM, AU Commission, EU EPF, EU NAVFOR, Combined Maritime Forces, UN Monitoring Group, World Bank, IPC, FDD, ISS Africa, ICG, CTC West Point, Grey Dynamics, Pakistan Today, Express Tribune, Ansar Burney Trust, polity.org.za, Hiiraan Online, Garowe Online, WardheerNews, Addis Standard, CFR, Kormeeraha, Horseed Media, Middle East Monitor, Maritime Executive, TIME, and major international outlets.
